one_liner: Header-only C++17 JSON library, 2-4x faster than nlohmann::json at parsing and serializing; RapidJSON still wins parsing.
what_it_does: utl::json is a header-only DOM-style JSON parser/serializer, one module of the UTL header collection, with an nlohmann::json-like API (a Node class, from_string/from_file, to_string/to_file) but built directly on std::map/std::vector/std::string rather than custom containers. It supports full UTF-8 output and UTF-16-surrogate-pair \u escape handling, exception-based validation, and macro-driven recursive struct reflection (UTL_JSON_REFLECT) for direct struct<->JSON conversion. It is API-similar to nlohmann::json but not source-compatible (different class/method names).
how_it_is_fast: Single-pass recursive-descent parser with no separate tokenizing stage: node type is decided from the first character inside Parser::parse_node(), so the document is scanned once while the recursive Node tree is built. Numbers go through std::charconv's from_chars/to_chars, with a locale-based istringstream fallback only on libc++ <20 (no floating-point from_chars there). The header's own dev docs state it uses no intrinsics or compiler-specific code anywhere, so the win over nlohmann comes from a leaner single-scan design and std::charconv, not vectorization -- which is also why hand-tuned RapidJSON still beats it on most parsing runs.
when_to_use: Already modeling data with std::map/std::vector/std::string and want JSON that interoperates with those containers directly, no custom container API to learn
Want recursive struct<->JSON reflection (UTL_JSON_REFLECT macro) without hand-writing serializers
Currently on nlohmann::json and want a similarly-shaped, header-only replacement that's 2.2-4x faster parsing and 1.6-2.4x faster serializing, without needing RapidJSON/simdjson-class throughput
Need a tiny dependency footprint: single header, under 1k lines, MIT, no third-party deps
Workload looks like the benchmarked files (twitter.json/apache_builds.json/strings.json/numbers.json shape) rather than deeply object-keyed documents
when_not_to_use: Baseline to beat is RapidJSON, not nlohmann: RapidJSON parses faster on 3 of 4 benchmarked files (numbers.json, twitter.json, apache_builds.json), only strings.json parsing favors utl::json
Object-heavy / heavily-keyed documents: object_type is std::map, so map insertion/iteration dominates runtime -- the author names this the library's main perf weak point
Need SIMD-class throughput (simdjson, Glaze, yyjson): utl::json deliberately avoids intrinsics and compiler-specific code for portability, at the cost of top-end speed
Need distinct integer vs float JSON numbers: number_type is a single double for every JSON number (open, unaddressed feature request #2), so integers beyond 2^53 lose precision

Building with Clang + libc++ < 20: falls back to a much slower locale-based istringstream number parser (check UTL_JSON_FROM_CHARS_FALLBACK), narrowing or erasing the published speedup on that toolchain (mostly a macOS issue)

integration.dependencies: none (self-contained single header; nlohmann/PicoJSON/RapidJSON are only benchmark-harness comparisons, not runtime deps)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17; MSVC needs /Zc:preprocessor for the UTL_JSON_REFLECT macro to expand correctly
integration.platforms: any -- CI covers Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, FreeBSD; no intrinsics or architecture-specific code in the parser
integration.thread_safety: Not documented for Node/Parser directly. The header notes its libc++ from_chars fallback is specifically 'thread-safe locale-neutral' (avoiding stod/strtod's global-locale issues), implying the rest of the parser holds no shared mutable state, but no explicit thread-safety guarantee is given.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — API shape mirrors nlohmann::json (Node vs json, from_string/to_string) but names and methods differ, so call sites need porting, not just a header swap

gotchas: object_type is std::map<std::string, Node, std::less<>> — object-heavy JSON pays std::map insertion/iteration cost; documented as the main performance weak point
number_type is one double for every JSON number, no separate integer type; a feature request for int/float split is open and unresolved (issue #2)
from_string()/from_file() default recursion_limit=100 to cap stack depth against maliciously deep nesting, throwing std::runtime_error past the limit — raise it if legitimate documents nest deeper
Clang + libc++ <20 silently swaps in a slower locale-based float parser (no std::from_chars); detect with #ifdef UTL_JSON_FROM_CHARS_FALLBACK before trusting benchmark numbers on that toolchain
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick utl::json over cjson.cpp / json.cpp / DAW JSON Link / Tachyon.JSON when the goal is STL-container-backed Node values plus macro-based recursive struct reflection in one sub-1k-line header; pick one of those siblings instead when the target baseline is RapidJSON or simdjson rather than nlohmann, since utl::json's wins are consistent only against nlohmann::json and PicoJSON.
verified_claims_summary: First-party nanobench tables in docs/module_json.md (no compiler, flags, or CPU model given) show utl::json parsing 2.2x faster than nlohmann::json on twitter.json (402.89 vs 182.76 op/s) and 2.4x on apache_builds.json (2,134.76 vs 881.03 op/s), and serializing 1.6-1.9x faster on those same files. RapidJSON parses faster than utl::json on numbers.json (1.29-1.45x), twitter.json (2.07-2.22x), apache_builds.json (1.63-1.72x) and database.json (1.30-1.40x), and roughly ties it at serializing apache_builds.json.
status_note: Actively developed (repo pushed 2026-09-19) but the published master branch — what a consumer actually pulls — last moved 2025-12-08; MIT-licensed, 336 stars, not a fork, small enough to vendor as one header.
